answers.answer: 1) Three pods. 2) Randomly selected; lowest number in A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. 3) 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus one additional Adult per player.
answers.evidence: [1] For 3–4 players, 3 Escape Pod tokens are selected. [2] Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section A, the next (in numerical order) in Section B, then alternate A/B; all pods start Locked side face up. [3] Put in the bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.

answers.answer: 1) Remove cards for player counts above the actual count, shuffle Corporate and Personal decks separately, and deal one of each to every player. 2) Choose one of the two at the First Encounter, when an Intruder first appears. 3) Remove the rejected card face down from the game; players cannot inspect others' removed Objectives. 4) Eggs do not trigger the choice; they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: [1] Remove from both Objective decks all cards showing a player count higher than the actual number of players; shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden. [2-3] The first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). [4] Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.

answers.answer: 1) Discard the played card plus two other Action cards, three Action cards total. The held card itself is among the cards discarded. 2) No: Contamination cards are never Action-cost payment. 3) Choose one of the OR sections; pay the printed cost for that chosen action plus the played card.
answers.evidence: [1] For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total. [2] Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost. [3] If a card has two sections separated by OR, choose one.

answers.answer: 1) Take one Light Wound at the end of your own round, after your Action and pass. 2) Passing ends your normal Actions for that Player Phase. 3) At passing, you may discard any number of hand cards. 4) No further Fire wound that turn: later players' rounds do not apply to you.
answers.evidence: [1,4] A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn). [2] After you pass, you cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted. [3] At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.

answers.answer: 1) Flip the Room tile face up, resolve and remove its Exploration token, and orient the tile so its token's number faces the board Item Counter. Nest and Slime Room have no Item count. 2) Resolve the symbol effect; Door places in the Corridor used to enter. 3) For an empty destination, make a Noise roll and place a numbered marker in the connected Corridor (or Technical Corridors space if applicable); Danger instead moves all eligible neighboring Intruders, or places markers in all clear connected Corridors if none eligible. 4) Silence replaces the roll; Slime converts Silence to Danger. An already occupied destination skips the ordinary Movement Noise roll.
answers.evidence: [1] After entering a Room, if the tile was unexplored, flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box. The Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other tiles, rotate until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol. [2] Doors — place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered. [3] A numbered Noise result places a marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). Danger moves all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room; if none are eligible, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one. [4] A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise afterward. Never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve Silence as Danger.

answers.answer: 1) Cost 2 Action cards; it follows normal Movement restrictions and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to destination. 2) Forbidden in Combat and if all destination-connected Corridors already have Noise. 3) Closed Doors block movement; miniatures cannot stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: [1] Careful Movement (cost 2) follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. [2] You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. [3] Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor. A Closed Door blocks the neighboring status for players' Movement.

answers.answer: 1) The Encounter first discards all Noise markers in connected Corridors, including Technical Corridors if connected, then draws a bag token and places a matching miniature unless Blank. 2) Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; a later Technical Corridors hiding event returns it to bag. 3) Compare token number with all cards in triggering hand: fewer cards than number means Surprise Attack; equal or more means none. 4) Contamination cards count toward hand size.
answers.evidence: [1] Resolve an Encounter: discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance); draw 1 Intruder token from the bag; place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. [2] Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it may return if an Intruder of that type later hides by entering Technical Corridors. [3-4] Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number means Surprise Attack; equal or more means nothing happens.

requested_parts: movement into your Room as Encounter
answers.answer: 1) All eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms move into the Room. 2) If none are eligible, place Noise in every connected Corridor lacking one, counting Technical Corridors where the Room has an Entrance. 3) Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. 4) A Character with Slime treats Silence as Danger.
answers.evidence: [1-2] Danger moves ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. [3] An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter. [4] If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve Silence as Danger.

answers.answer: 1) Place Noise in each Corridor connected to the Room; return Blank to bag; no miniature appears and Encounter ends. 2) If Blank was the last token in bag, add an Adult token if available. 3) In bag development, Blank adds an Adult if available and then returns to bag; there is no Encounter Noise placement in that branch.
answers.evidence: [1-2] Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag, add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears). [3] Blank bag development adds 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens) and returns the Blank token to the bag.

requested_parts: movement through Closed Door and endpoints
answers.answer: 1) Both Intruders stay in their original Room; the first attempts block and destroy the Closed Door, with both staying put. 2) Door becomes Destroyed; only Plasma Torch can close a Destroyed Door. 3) An Intruder appearing from a Noise roll comes through a Closed Door regardless of it.
answers.evidence: [1] An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). [2] Destroyed = lying token; movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. [3] If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.

answers.answer: 1) Remove miniature from board and return its token to the bag; discard all its Injury markers. 2) The existing Noise marker stays. 3) Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors (except Mechanic's Technical Corridors card and Technical Corridor Plans); Doors can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: [1-2] If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this. [3] Characters can never use Technical Corridors (the only exceptions: the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and the Technical Corridor Plans Item card). Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: 1) Shoot costs one Action card and one Ammo: choose a Weapon and Intruder in your Room, spend Ammo, roll die. 2) Melee costs one Action card and draws one Contamination card onto your Action discard, then targets an Intruder in your Room and rolls. 3) Shoot miss is zero Injury and no shooter Wound; Melee miss is zero Injury plus one Serious Wound to attacker. 4) Double hit deals 2 Injuries shooting and 1 in Melee.
answers.evidence: [1] Shoot (cost 1): requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo; choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room; discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon card; roll the Combat die. [2] Melee Attack (cost 1): draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; roll the Combat die. [3] A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker. [4] Double-hit symbol: 2 Injuries before Weapon modifiers for Shoot; 1 Injury for Melee.

answers.answer: 1) One Injury kills a Larva. 2) Adult draws one Intruder Attack card and dies if blood value is no greater than its total Injuries. 3) Queen draws two cards and sums blood; sum no greater than total Injuries kills; a Retreat arrow on either card makes it retreat instead of numerical death check. 4) A Carcass is placed for dead Creeper, Adult, Breeder or Queen, not Larva.
answers.evidence: [1] Larva: 1 Injury kills. [2] Adult: draw 1 Intruder Attack card; Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. [3] Queen: draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. If any drawn card's blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result; the Queen retreats if either of its 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol. [4] On death, a Larva has no Carcass; Creeper, Adult, Breeder and Queen place a Carcass in the Room.

answers.answer: 1) Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack for each Intruder in the Room, largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. 2) Escape attack targets the escaper. 3) If they die, the Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. 4) If they survive, complete the move into the neighboring unexplored Room and explore/roll Noise normally, if destination is empty.
answers.evidence: [1] Before moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). [2] An Escape attack targets the escaper. [3-4] If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.

answers.answer: 1) Intruder targets Character with fewest Action cards in hand; tie goes to First Player token holder, or next in turn order. 2) Draw Attack card; matching Intruder symbol resolves effect, otherwise miss; ignore blood icon. 3) Larva draws no Attack card; it Infests. 4) Target gains one Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: [1] With several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand is attacked; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order). [2] For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks. [3] A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead remove it from the board and place it on the target Character board. [4] The target gains 1 Contamination card; when a Character gets one, place it on top of their Action discard pile.

requested_parts: dressed Serious Wound at three and Light Wound
answers.answer: 1) No: dressing ignores the card effect but it still counts toward three, so any further Wound kills at three Serious Wounds. 2) A third Light Wound clears the Light track and causes a Serious Wound. 3) Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound as specified. 4) On death place Corpse in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: [1] Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds; a dressed Serious Wound still counts toward the 3-wound limit. [2] On a 3rd Light Wound, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound. [3] Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. [4] Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room, and drop all their Heavy Objects there.

answers.answer: 1) Canteen/Shower scan only Contamination cards in hand; remove non-Infected cards. 2) Infected card stays; with no existing Larva place one; with Larva already present Character dies and a Creeper is placed in Room. 3) Surgery scans all Contamination in deck, hand and discard; removes Infected cards and a Larva if present, then costs one Light Wound. 4) Surgery automatically passes and shuffles all cards, including hand, into Action deck, leaving hand empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: [1] Canteen and Shower scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones. [2] Infected → Larva; with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room. [3-4] Surgery: Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.

answers.answer: 1) Shoot or Melee destroys one uncarried Egg per Injury; Grenade destroys two; Molotov immediately destroys one; Fire destroys one per Event Phase Fire Damage step (two in Nest with Vulnerability to Fire). 2) Successful Egg Melee retains Contamination draw; missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound, though draw timing is unresolved. 3) Roll Noise after every attempt including miss; remote explosives roll in your own Room. 4) When no Eggs remain on Intruder board, Nest is destroyed and marked with one Injury.
answers.evidence: [1] Shoot or Melee: each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs. Molotov Cocktail destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. Fire normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step; for the Nest Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2. [2] A successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card; a missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll draw with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified. [3] After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest. [4] When no Eggs remain (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.

answers.answer: 1) Pay two Action cards for the relevant Section Room Action; Pod must be unlocked and have space; no Intruder or Malfunction in Section. Roll Noise first; if Intruder appears or is present, entry fails. 2) Two Characters fit per Pod; Heavy Objects take no character space. 3) After boarding, may launch immediately; otherwise wait/pass, and in later Player Phases choose wait/pass, launch, or exit free and take a full two-Action round. 4) Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants to Room; a Malfunction does not stop current waiting, launch or exit, only new entry.
answers.evidence: [1] Pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. [2] Capacity: 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space. [3] After boarding you may launch immediately. If waiting, you pass the current turn. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions. [4] An Intruder appears in the Section while you wait: all Characters in that Section's Pods immediately return to its Room. A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait: you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods.

answers.answer: 1) Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. 2) Two or three Damaged Engines explode ship; everyone aboard dies, but launched passengers are away. 3) Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters; Quarantine sleeper survives if destination Mars. 4) If scan finds Infected or Larva already exists, shuffle all Action/Contamination cards across deck, hand and discard and draw four; any Contamination among four kills. 5) Yes, launched Pod passengers also undergo Contamination check.
answers.evidence: [1] Resolve Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives. [2] 2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. Launched Pod passengers are already away. [3] Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if destination is Mars. [4-5] For every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers: if at least one Infected card or a Larva already on board, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard into one Action deck and draw top 4; any Contamination among those four kills you.

answers.answer: 1) Shuffle all Room 2 tiles unseen and place one on each 2 slot, return extras unseen; do same for all Room 1 tiles. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen and place one face down on each Room; return extras. 2) One random Coordinates card face down by Cockpit; Destination marker on B; Time marker on green space. 3) Each Engine gets a shuffled face-down Working and Damaged token stack. 4) Intruder board gets five Egg tokens and three random Weakness cards face down.
answers.evidence: [1] Shuffle all Room tiles 2 without looking at fronts and randomly place one face down on each slot marked 2; return the rest unseen. Place all Room tiles 1 the same way on slots marked 1. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, place one face down on each Room tile, return the rest. [2] Place 1 random Coordinates card face down next to Cockpit; put Destination marker on B; put Time marker on green space. [3] For each Engine, shuffle its Damaged and Working tokens face down and stack on matching slot; top indicates true status. [4] Place 5 Egg tokens and 3 random Weakness cards face down in their slots.

answers.answer: 1) Randomly deal numbered Help cards for player count; these assign Player Numbers. In that order draw two Character draft cards, reveal both, choose one, shuffle unchosen back before next draw. 2) Each gets Help card, matching Inventory, board, miniature, shuffled 10 Action deck, loaded starting Weapon, and two horizontal inactive Quest Items. 3) Characters start in Hibernatorium; initial blue Corpse is also placed there. 4) Quest Items are not active at start; fulfill mini-quest to activate.
answers.evidence: [1] Randomly deal Player Numbers using Help cards 1 to player count. In Player Number order each player draws 2 draft cards, reveals both publicly, chooses 1, and shuffles the unchosen card back before next draw. [2] Take Help card and matching Inventory holder, Character board and miniature, 10-card Action deck, Starting Item Weapon loaded to its capacity, and 2 Quest Items horizontal side up. [3] The miniature is placed in the Hibernatorium; place the blue Character Corpse token in the Hibernatorium. [4] Quest Items are NOT active at the start — they unlock via mini-quests.

answers.answer: 1) At Player Phase start everyone draws to five (six with Cabins). 2) After drawing, pass First Player token left except first game turn. 3) When deck empty for required draw, shuffle discard into a new deck and draw. 4) Normal card discards are face up; Action and gained Contamination go to own Action discard, Items to matching discard, Event/Attack/Serious Wound to respective piles. Explicit exceptions: search rejected card face down bottom of deck.
answers.evidence: [1] Every player draws from their Action deck up to a hand of 5 cards; Cabins gives a hand of 6. [2] After drawing, pass First Player token to the player on the left; do not pass it on the first turn. [3] Whenever you must draw and your Action deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck, then draw. [4] Normal card discards are face up; Action and gained Contamination cards go to that Character's Action discard pile; Items to matching Item discard; Event, Intruder Attack and Serious Wound cards to their own discard piles. Search/Storage return rejected card face down to bottom of chosen deck.

requested_parts: Intruders that move and movement controls
answers.answer: 1) Advance Time/Self-Destruct; Intruder Attacks; Fire Damage; Event movement then effect; bag development. 2) Intruders showing card symbol and not in Room with Characters move to neighboring Room through Corridor matching number; Technical Corridor result removes them and returns token to bag. 3) Resolve event effect after movement. 4) Empty Event deck reshuffles Event discards; empty Intruder Attack deck reshuffles its discard.
answers.evidence: [1] Complete order: advance Time/Self-Destruct → Intruder Attacks → Fire Damage → Event card (movement, then effect) → Intruder bag development. [2] All Intruders showing card's symbol that are NOT in a Room with Characters move to neighboring Room through Corridor matching card number; a Technical Corridor number removes miniature and returns token to bag. [3] After movement, resolve the Event effect. [4] If Event deck runs out, shuffle Event discards into a new deck. If Intruder Attack deck runs out, reshuffle its discard into a new deck.

requested_parts: token returns and Noise roll timing
answers.answer: 1) Larva removed from bag and an Adult added; Creeper removed and a Breeder added. 2) Adult returned immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Combat; Breeder has all roll first, then returns. 3) Queen in Nest places Queen and resolves Encounter; otherwise add Egg to board; return Queen. 4) Adult Encounter can draw that just returned Adult. After all branch procedures, next turn begins.
answers.evidence: [1] Larva: remove token from bag; add 1 Adult. Creeper: remove token; add 1 Breeder. [2] Adult: return token immediately before all players roll Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat); Breeder: all players roll Noise in order, then return Breeder. [3] Queen: if any Characters in Nest, place Queen miniature and resolve Encounter; if no Characters there or it is undiscovered, add 1 Egg to board. Return token to bag. [4] An Encounter from Adult development rolls may draw that same Adult token. Finish all consequences of bag development before next turn's Player Phase.

answers.answer: 1) Instructed placement of a ninth Fire or Malfunction marker ends game via ship explosion/hull loss. 2) Each type max one per Room; extra placement in already marked Room does nothing; discarded markers return to pool. 3) Ship explosion kills everyone and everything aboard including sleeping Characters and Intruders. 4) Hull loss ends game immediately.
answers.evidence: [1] If instructed to place a 9th Fire marker, or a 9th Malfunction marker, the ship explodes/loses hull integrity and the game ends. [2] Fire and Malfunction each max 1 per Room; extra placements do nothing; discarded markers return to pool. [3] Ship explosion: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders. [4] A 9th Malfunction placement causes loss of hull integrity and game end.

answers.answer: 1) Malfunction disables Room Action and Computer; Search remains usable. 2) Never placed in Nest, Slime Room, or unexplored Room. 3) It does not change Engine token status; a Hibernatorium Malfunction does not affect already hibernating Characters.
answers.evidence: [1] Malfunction makes the Room's Action unavailable (Searching still works) and makes its Computer unavailable. [2] Malfunction markers are never placed in Nest or Room Covered in Slime; they cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms. [3] They do not affect Engine status, only Room Action; Malfunction in Hibernatorium doesn't affect already-hibernated Characters.

answers.answer: 1) Normal Item cards are hidden in Inventory; others see backs/colors. No Inventory size limit; any Item used must be shown. 2) Heavy Items/Objects are public and occupy one of two Hand slots; third requires dropping one. 3) Heavy Items found by search do not need Pick Up; Heavy Objects do. 4) Add Items attach to another card and act as one; Duct Tape combines two Heavy Item cards into one hand slot, not Heavy Objects.
answers.evidence: [1] Normal Item cards are hidden in card holder — others see only backs/colors. No Inventory size limit. Any Item used must be shown to all players. [2] Heavy Items and Objects are never hidden; each occupies one of your 2 Hand slots. To take a third, Drop one first. [3] Heavy Objects include Eggs, Character Corpses, Intruder Carcasses; Pick Up Heavy Object applies to Objects only; Heavy Items found by Searching do not require this Action. [4] Add-type Items attach to another card and act as one. Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy Item cards into one unit occupying 1 Hand slot; it cannot combine Heavy Objects.

requested_parts: voluntary Item and Object drop outcomes
answers.answer: 1) Dropped Objects stay in Room; dropped Items are lost/discarded. 2) Drop is free at any time during your turn, no Action. 3) Weapon found by Searching starts with one Ammo; starting Weapon is loaded to printed capacity.
answers.evidence: [1] Dropped Objects stay in the Room; dropped Items are lost (discarded). [2] Drop is free, any time during your turn, no Action. [3] A Weapon found by Searching starts with 1 Ammo. Starting Weapon is loaded with Ammo markers equal to that Weapon's Ammo capacity.

requested_parts: zero Items, Special Rooms, Blue Items
answers.answer: 1) Search uses deck matching Room color; white Room lets you choose any Red/Yellow/Green deck. 2) Draw two from one deck, keep one, return other face down to bottom, no shuffle. 3) Each Search lowers Item Counter by one. 4) At zero ordinary Search unavailable except Scout Scavenging; Special Rooms Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines cannot be searched; Nest and Slime Room forbid Search; Blue items are crafted, never searched.
answers.evidence: [1] Match Room color; in a white Room choose any of the 3 decks. Blue Items are Crafted and never found by Searching. [2] Draw 2 cards from one deck, keep 1, return other face down to bottom of that deck, without shuffling. [3] In other Rooms, each Search lowers Item Counter by 1; at 0 Room cannot be searched. [4] Exception: Scout's Scavenging. Special Rooms Hibernatorium, Cockpit and Engines 1–3 cannot be Searched; Nest and Room Covered With Slime prohibit any Search Action.

answers.answer: 1) Pay one Action card and discard two Item cards showing matching blue component icons. 2) Crafted result must be available. 3) You may inspect Craft deck at any time. 4) Antidote flame+medical cross; Taser battery/lightning+tool; Flamethrower flame+tool; Molotov flame+fabric.
answers.evidence: [1] To Craft, pay 1 Action card plus 2 matching Item components; discard those Items and take the Crafted Item whose gray icons match their blue icons. [2] A Crafted Item cannot be built if its card is not available. [3] You may look through Craft deck at any time. [4] Crafted items and symbols: Antidote = flame + medical cross; Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric.

answers.answer: 1) Only initiator pays; any Characters in Room may trade with one another if they agree. 2) Yes, you may give Item/Object for nothing, but no empty action with no intention to trade; honest negotiation may fail. 3) Ammo cannot be exchanged. 4) Heavy Items found by Searching need no separate Pick Up; pickup action is for Objects.
answers.evidence: [1] Trade with all Characters in your Room; only initiator spends Action. Any Characters in Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay. [2] You may give an Item/Object for nothing; empty Actions with no meaningful game-state change, including Trade with no intention of exchange, are disallowed. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. [3] Characters cannot exchange Ammo. [4] Heavy Items found by Searching do not require Pick Up Action; it applies to Objects only.

answers.answer: 1) Corresponding objects are Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg. 2) Object must be present in Laboratory Room. 3) Reveal corresponding Weakness face up; leave it on board; Object not consumed; benefit applies to all players. 4) Discover Weakness Objective can be satisfied by anyone's research before game end.
answers.evidence: [1-3] Laboratory: Analyse 1 Object (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg present in the Room): reveal corresponding Weakness face up and leave it on Intruder board. Its rule benefits all players. The Object is not consumed. [4] Discover a Weakness: a corresponding Object must be researched in the Laboratory by anyone before game end.

answers.answer: 1) Character must be in that Room, out of Combat, no Malfunction, and pay two Action cards. 2) Computer icon itself grants no action or benefit; it only matters when another rule refers to Computer. Malfunction makes unavailable. 3) Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Search.
answers.evidence: [1] Room Actions cost 2 Action cards; Character must be in the Room whose Action is used. Cannot perform while in Combat or in Room with Malfunction. [2] Computer icon identifies a Computer but grants no independent Action or benefit; matters only when another rule refers to it. Malfunction makes it unavailable. [3] Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms.

answers.answer: 1) Armory adds Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons. 2) Two Ammo. 3) Cannot recharge Classic Weapons or exceed capacity.

answers.answer: 1) No, not automatically after every player has had one round; continue Player rounds while anyone active. 2) Start First Player clockwise, each active unpassed player takes two Actions; repeat rounds in that order skipping passed players. 3) If taking only one Action, must pass; if unable or choosing not to act, pass. 4) Player Phase ends only when everyone has passed.
answers.evidence: [1-2] Starting with First Player and going clockwise, each active player who has not passed performs a round of 2 Actions. Repeat rounds in that order, skipping passed players, while anyone remains active. [3] If perform only 1 Action instead of two, must pass; if cannot perform Actions or choose not to, must pass. [4] Only when everyone has passed does Player Phase end and Event Phase begin.
